title: Matchmaking algorithm behind a refreshed flag snapshot
name: Matchmaking flag switch

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code evaluates feature flags when flag data is missing? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The flag service goes down for ten minutes after the server has started successfully. How does GameFlags behave during the outage?
choices: It clears the snapshot so every flag reads from its default
It keeps serving the last successfully fetched snapshot and logs a warning on each failed refresh
It stops the refresh timer after the first failure
It throws from isOn until the service recovers

questions.prompt: The flag source briefly serves a cached older response with a lower version number than the one already loaded. What happens?
choices: The older snapshot replaces the newer one
refresh() throws and the timer stops
The older snapshot is ignored because its version is lower
Both snapshots are merged flag by flag

questions.prompt: matchmaking_skill_v2 is flipped on while formMatches is in the middle of processing a large queue. Which algorithm is used for that call?
choices: The value read at the start of the call is used for every region in that call
Regions processed after the flip use skill_v2, earlier ones use legacy
Matches are labelled skill_v2 but ordered with the legacy sort
The call is aborted and retried
